claims.claim: (a) In 11.0.0 the browser client records a session hit by an uncaught error as 'unhandled', never 'crashed'
claims.evidence: getsentry/sentry-javascript @ 11.0.0 (commit 3e02c87c), fetched first-hand with gh api; cached scratchpad copies were byte-identical: packages/browser/src/client.ts:111-112 — comment 'Unhandled errors don't actually crash the browser, so we report `unhandled` rather than `crashed`.' then `this._unhandledSessionStatus = 'unhandled';`. The core default is 'crashed' (packages/core/src/client.ts:224-230, :252), and the browser client overrides it. A grep of the browser, browser-utils and core sources finds no other path that marks a browser session crashed. MIGRATION.md:561-565 'Browser sessions use `unhandled` instead of `crashed`', warning that crash-free rates will shift. Session status type: packages/core/src/types/session.ts:33.

claims.claim: (b) A captureException call is handled by default and only marks the session 'errored'
claims.evidence: packages/browser/src/eventbuilder.ts:232 `addExceptionMechanism(event); // defaults to { type: 'generic', handled: true }`; packages/core/src/utils/misc.ts:136-139. packages/core/src/client.ts:1338-1368 `_updateSessionFromEvent`: an exception sets errored=true. The status changes only when `mechanism.handled === false`; otherwise it just sets errors: 1, and the server counts that as errored (the SDK type has no 'errored' status). The session update runs only after beforeSend keeps the event (client.ts:1543-1557), so dropped engine noise never touches the session. Sentry's Next.js release docs (fetched 2026-10-03) agree: errored when an event with an exception is captured; unhandled when an error reaches the global handler, which was crashed before SDK 11.

claims.claim: (c) How a manual capture is marked unhandled in v11: `captureException(err, { mechanism: { handled: false } })` — field name, and that it flips the session to 'unhandled'
claims.evidence: EventHint has `mechanism?: Partial<Mechanism>` (packages/core/src/types/event.ts:82). packages/core/src/utils/prepareEvent.ts:77-78 applies hint.mechanism to the captured exception (misc.ts:123-139), then client.ts:1350-1352 sets unhandled, and :1365 sets status to `this._unhandledSessionStatus` ('unhandled' in the browser). CAVEAT: captureException parses its 2nd argument with parseEventHintOrCaptureContext (exports.ts:26-28; prepareEvent.ts:335-373). An object carrying any ScopeContext key (user, level, extra, contexts, tags, fingerprint, propagationContext) is treated as a capture context, so `mechanism` is silently dropped. TypeScript's ExclusiveEventHintOrCaptureContext (prepareEvent.ts:25-27) rejects the mix. reportError's code tag and level must go through `captureContext` inside the hint, or withScope.

### 3.2 The names filter

```ts
// web/lib/monitoring/scrub.ts
export function rememberOpenFile(fileName: string): void; // called when a file is picked
export function rememberScore(score: ScoreFacts): void; // title, subtitle, artist, album, words,
// music, copyright, tab author, and every track's name and short name
```

- **The list never forgets** within a tab. A breadcrumb about file A can still be in the trail after
  file B opens.
- **Strings shorter than 3 characters are skipped**, so a track named `1` does not rewrite unrelated
  text.
- **Both ends:** breadcrumbs are filtered when they are recorded (`beforeBreadcrumb`), and the whole
  event again when it is sent (`beforeSend`), which also covers names registered after a breadcrumb
  was recorded.
- **Stack frames are not touched.** File paths in frames are our code, not the visitor's.

before_verbatim.text:
### 2.5 The lint rule

Two selectors make a catch that reports nothing a lint error. Both were run against a scratch file
on 2026-10-03 with the installed ESLint 9.39.4: they flagged exactly `catch { }` and
`.catch(() => null)`, and passed every form that calls `reportError` or `noteError`.

```js
{ selector: 'CatchClause:not(:has(CallExpression[callee.name=/^(reportError|noteError)$/]))', … },
{ selector: "CallExpression[callee.property.name='catch'] > :function:not(:has(CallExpression[callee.name=/^(reportError|noteError)$/]))", … },
```

- **They join the existing `no-restricted-syntax` list** at `web/eslint.config.mjs:68`. A second
  block that sets the same rule would silently replace the AlphaTab dynamic-import fence already
  there. If the new selectors need a narrower `files` scope (test files are exempt), that block must
  repeat the fence's selector, held in a shared constant.
- **A deliberate silence** is `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax -- <reason>`. The
  repository already requires a reason on every disable comment
  (`eslint-comments/require-description`).

- **Lint canary:** a test runs ESLint over a silent `catch { }` and expects it to fail, so the rule
  cannot stop working quietly — the same idea as `tooling/check-core-purity-canary.sh`.

spike.what: web/node_modules/.bin/eslint 9.39.4 with @typescript-eslint/parser 8.61.1 (the worktree's install) over three probes in scratchpad verify-A/lint-16/: (1) imports reportError from './report' and calls it in a catch; (2) calls reportError(error) in a catch with no import; (3) silent `catch { }`. Config: the two section 2.5 selectors, verbatim, plus no-restricted-globals for reportError. Run twice: parser default lib, and lib [dom, dom.iterable, esnext]. A control run used the selectors only.

Import reportError from web/lib/monitoring/report.ts."). Probe 3: flagged ONLY by no-restricted-syntax (line 4, the CatchClause selector). notes: At runtime the global reportError reports the exception to window (HTML 'report an exception'), so Sentry's GlobalHandlers would capture it as UNHANDLED with its full message: no code tag, no E101-E103 message drop, and the session marked unhandled (reasoned, untested). no-restricted-globals does not catch member calls such as globalThis.reportError(…) or window.reportError(…). unicorn/prefer-global-this is on in web/ and steers code toward globalThis.x, so add no-restricted-properties if that form matters.
